clues: This was first documented by autopsy in 1871 and later called Wilkie's Syndrome after a British surgeon, David Wilkie, published a major 1927 case series of 75 patients.

In the mid-20th century, doctors frequently diagnosed this condition in teenagers and young adults recovering from spinal surgery for scoliosis in part due to the postoperative spine lengthening. Interestingly, patients found relief of their abdominal pain by lying on their left side, in a prone position, or pulling their knees to their chest

In addition to prior surgery increasing the risk of this condition, it is now most often seen after rapid weight loss for any reason due to the loss of mesenteric fat leading the aortomesenteric angle to narrow to less than 15 degrees

Approximately 25% of people who are allergic to cats or dogs are actually reacting to this substance, rather than the animal's fur. Rarely, some highly cat-allergic individuals can actually experience severe allergic reactions when eating pork, a bizarre cross-reactivity known as Pork-Cat syndrome

As the US prepared to enter World War II, the military wanted to develop a stable, compact blood substitute to treat battlefield shock and burns. Because this substance is found in most vertebrates, scientists initially believed human and bovine versions of this substance were identical enough and began clinical trials on inmates at Norfolk State Prison Colony and Harvard Medical Students. This triggered severe, delayed serum sickness and the bovine military program was permanently shut down.
Providing approximately 80% of the colloid osmotic pressure in blood vessels, this protein folds into a distinct heart-shaped conformation

Traditional healers in Madagascar and Southern Africa used rosy periwinkle (catharanthus roseus) for various folk remedies such as treating diabetes. Researchers studying this plant found numerous alkaloids with no blood sugar lowering effect but isolated and developed this medication in 1961, which is now on the WHO list of essential medications

Originally, this medication was exceptionally expensive as it required roughly one ton of dried periwinkle leaves to yield just one ounce of the drug, although now it is made semi-synthetically and remains a core part of pediatric cancer care
Commonly causing peripheral neuropathy, this medication works by binding to tubulin and preventing mitosis

Evidence of this disease has been found in a 4,000-year-old skeleton in India and ancient Egyptian remains. Historians believe that members of Alexander the Great's army contracted the disease during their invasion of India in the 4th century BCE and carried it back to the Mediterranean and the Middle East

Nine-banded armadillos and certain red squirrels are natural carriers of the bacteria that causes this disease. It has one of the longest incubation periods of any known disease with symptoms taking years to appear.

One of history's most famous figures with the disease was King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem, who successfully ruled the Crusader kingdom as a teenager and young adult. His tutor first noticed that he felt no pain while playing from a loss of sensation in his right arm. As the disease progressed, he developed blindness, facial disfigurement, and muscle weakness.

On the WHO list of essential medications, it can also be used to restore and rescue priceless works of art. For example, it was applied to wood panel paintings damaged as a results of the Arno River Flood of 1966 in Florence, Italy.
This medication is named after New York State where it was developed through a long distance collaboration between scientists in New York City and Albany
This medication binds to ergosterol, forming pores in the fungal cell membrane. It is available in oral suspensions, creams, ointments, and powders.
